page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m1.4xlarge is a burstable virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a 1.0 GB per core allocation. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and 10% respectively, and single-threaded gzip compression rated as poor. However, multi-core performance is average, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth remains average for both read and write operations, though the overall Passmark memory score is weak. The instance handles static web serving, Redis SET operations, and small-model LLM prompt processing at average speeds, but struggles with larger 7B LLM models.

Due to its burstable CPU allocation and low memory-to-vCPU ratio, this instance offers a cost-effective option for workloads with variable CPU utilization. It is designed for scenarios that experience periodic traffic spikes rather than sustained high-intensity processing. Suitable workloads include static web serving, software compilation, multi-threaded testing environments, and lightweight database operations that can leverage the 16 vCPUs during burst periods without exhausting CPU credits.
